Run Association Analysis

Source: R/run_association.R
run_association.Rd

Perform GLM-based association testing between a specified outcome and features from exposures, omics, or latent factors. Each feature is tested in its own model, built from a user-supplied formula. Models can be run on subsets of samples, stratified by a grouping variable, or repeated across several formulas. Every fitted model is stored under a name so that specifications can be compared later with compare_association().

Usage

run_association(
  exposomicset,
  formula,
  source = c("omics", "exposures", "factors"),
  feature_set = NULL,
  log_trans = TRUE,
  top_n = NULL,
  family = "gaussian",
  correction_method = "fdr",
  subset = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  action = "add",
  feature_col = NULL,
  mirna_assays = NULL
)

Arguments

exposomicset

A MultiAssayExperiment object containing data and metadata.

formula

A two-sided formula whose left-hand side is a single column of colData (the outcome) and whose right-hand side contains the covariates, e.g. smoker ~ age * sex. Each feature is added to the model as a main effect. To control how the feature enters the model (for example to test an interaction), use the placeholder .feature on the right-hand side, e.g. smoker ~ .feature * sex + age. Use outcome ~ 1 for an unadjusted model. Alternatively, a named list of formulas (e.g. list(crude = y ~ 1, adjusted = y ~ age + sex)) fits every specification in one call, each stored under its list name.

source

Source of features to test. One of "omics", "exposures", "factors".

feature_set

Optional character vector of exposure or GO terms to test.

log_trans

Optional boolean value dictating whether or not to log2 transform omics features.

top_n

Optional integer: if using omics source, select top n most variable features.

family

GLM family; "gaussian" or "binomial".

correction_method

Method for p-value adjustment (default: "fdr"). Adjustment is performed separately for each model and each effect (see Value).

subset

Optional bare expression evaluated against the (unscaled) colData that selects the samples to model, e.g. sex == "female" or age > 40 & smoker == "no".

strata

Optional single column name of colData. The model is fit separately within each level and stored as [MODEL_NAME]_[LEVEL_IN_STRATA]. The stratifying variable must not appear in formula.

name

Optional name for the stored model. Defaults to "default", or to the text of subset when one is given. Ignored when formula is a named list (the list names are used).

overwrite

Logical; if TRUE, replace an existing model with the same name instead of erroring or appending features to it (default: FALSE).

action

If "add" (default), saves results to metadata; else returns results as list.

feature_col

The column in rowData for matching gene symbols or IDs.

mirna_assays

Optional character vector of assays to exclude when extracting GO terms.

Value

If action = "add", returns updated MultiAssayExperiment. Otherwise, returns a list of:

  • models: a named list of fitted models, each containing results_df (tidy summary of associations), formula, covariates, family, subset, strata_var, stratum, and n_samples

  • model_data: the (full) data used in the GLMs

In results_df, term is the feature, coef is the model coefficient name, effect is "main" for the feature's main effect or the name of the interacting term (e.g. "sexMale"), and n / n_events give the observations (and binomial events) used.

Details

Numeric colData columns are z-scored once on the full sample before any subsetting, so effect sizes are on the same standardized scale in every subset and stratum and can be compared directly.

If a model with the same name already exists for the source and was fit with the same formula, subset, and family, new features are appended to it and p-values are re-adjusted across the combined set. A different specification under an existing name is an error unless overwrite = TRUE.

With strata, a stratum that cannot be fit (for example, a single outcome level or a constant covariate) is skipped with a warning.

Examples

# create example data
mae <- make_example_data(
    n_samples = 10,
    return_mae = TRUE
)
#> Ensuring all omics datasets are matrices with column names.
#> Creating SummarizedExperiment objects.
#> Creating MultiAssayExperiment object.
#> MultiAssayExperiment created successfully.

# covariate-adjusted main effect
mae <- mae |>
    run_association(
        formula = smoker ~ age,
        source = "exposures",
        feature_set = c("exposure_pm25", "exposure_no2"),
        family = "binomial"
    )
#> Running GLMs.

# several specifications at once
mae <- mae |>
    run_association(
        formula = list(
            crude = smoker ~ 1,
            adjusted = smoker ~ age
        ),
        source = "exposures",
        feature_set = c("exposure_pm25", "exposure_no2"),
        family = "binomial"
    )
#> Running GLMs.

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# subset of samples (assumes a `sex` column in colData)
mae <- mae |>
    run_association(
        formula = smoker ~ age,
        source = "exposures",
        feature_set = c("exposure_pm25", "exposure_no2"),
        family = "binomial",
        subset = sex == "female",
        name = "female"
    )

# stratified by sex, then compared
mae <- mae |>
    run_association(
        formula = smoker ~ age,
        source = "exposures",
        feature_set = c("exposure_pm25", "exposure_no2"),
        family = "binomial",
        strata = "sex",
        name = "by_sex"
    )

mae |>
    compare_association(
        source = "exposures",
        models = c("by_sex_female", "by_sex_male")
    )
} # }
